Thus, sixteen sections have been completed, according to their number and their law. In His wisdom, the Sages of the Talmud taught that one should believe only the good in them. Now, after these sections—short and long—we come to the explanation, in the season of Him who forms light, and I shall turn my hand to the laws mentioned above in the verse, "For God has made one opposite the other" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14</note> (meaning the sections and the laws of the shofar mentioned). I have made this, with the help of Heaven, to interpret them (the laws of the shofar mentioned) in accordance with the intention of the sections mentioned shortly hereafter. The general intention is one: it teaches sinners the way, according to the measure of the sections mentioned, both in brevity and in length.

## The law is that the shofar of Rosh Hashanah is ritually valid when made from a ram, etc., according to what is mentioned in the Gate of Holiness, because it is called the "penitent’s shofar" for two reasons mentioned there. It appears to me:

<margin>This is what is called a complete penitent, as our Sages stated (in the final chapter of Yoma): What is a "complete penitent"? For instance, one to whose hand an opportunity for transgression comes a first, second, and third time, and he is free from it in that same period (this is the strength of youth), with that same woman, and in that same place (this is the strength of the transgression). Therefore, their intention here is in his youth and his vigor; he is not free from the transgression due to old age or weakness of strength, but is a hero who conquers his impulse and separates himself.</margin>

The intention of our Sages in stating here "the shofar of Rosh Hashanah" (and calling it the shofar of Rosh Hashanah because it is the time appointed by the year to grasp his deeds and return to God, since repentance preceded the creation of the first man, as mentioned above in the text; and see that Rosh Hashanah is the beginning of the Ten Days of Repentance, so it is fitting to compare the penitent to the shofar of Rosh Hashanah) is that its mitzvah is with a ram. The essence of the mitzvah of a penitent is when he returns from his evil path, that he should return in the days of his youth, in his strength and his vigor. The ram mentioned here is from the expression "the ram <term>ayil</term> <gloss>ram/power</gloss> that butts" and from the expression "and he took the mighty <term>eilei</term> <gloss>rams/nobles</gloss> of the land" <note>2 Kings 24:15</note>, and from the expression "it is in the power <term>el</term> <gloss>power/strength</gloss> of my hand" <note>Genesis 31:29</note>, which means all are strength and vigor. They hinted at the strength of the forces, and also at the "strength of the transgression," meaning that the very transgression in which he stumbled in his youth is prepared before him, and he craves it, and it is in his power to do it as he did before, yet he is a hero who conquers his impulse and separates himself from it on account of repentance, not because of a failing of strength. For it looks identical in every way, and yet his impulse overcomes him and says to him, "Let us do it, it is a small thing," and he stands and answers with what he has already done, and so on.

## And it appears to me
That this is what they intended when they interpreted the verse "Happy is the man who fears the Lord" <note>Psalms 112:1</note> (and it was brought above in the Gate of Holiness): "A man, not a woman." Rav Amram said, "Happy is he who performs repentance while he is a man." And everyone says "Happy" is he who overcomes his impulse like a man. Rashi explains: "When he is a 'fire,' at the time when it burns with heat—meaning he hastens to extinguish it—or he preceded the days of old age, like a mighty man." It is possible that Rav did not come to disagree with Rav Amram, but to explain his words. He said that what Rav meant by "Happy is he who performs repentance while he is a man," his intention was when he is a youth as mentioned. He did not speak only of the strength of physical power, but spoke of the "strength of the transgression," for it is similar to before the fires of his passion, and he is not in this state because of compulsion, but because of God, and he is not seeking to chase after his impulse as at the beginning, but is a hero who conquers his impulse out of fear of sin. This is what Rav meant: he who overcomes his impulse, etc. Regarding this, it is fitting to say of him, "Happy is the man who fears the Lord," a complete penitent. And the Rav who said "while he is a man," meaning in his youth, said "Happy is the man" because he possesses two strengths: the strength of youth and the strength of conquering his impulse in that same period, with that same woman, etc. This whole principle is hinted at in the word *ayil*, which is a term for power and vigor. There is additional merit here: the strength of the *ayil* (ram) in terms of youthful vigor, and the strength of the "man" in terms of the transgression itself in that period and with that same woman, etc. Even if he bows his desire in this—according to our way, for the penitent must humble himself, be bowed, and crush his pride and haughtiness, and his soul should be like dust to all—this is the essence of repentance, as mentioned above in the Gate of Holiness. Our Sages came to inform us here, by stating "the shofar of Rosh Hashanah is valid when made from a ram" and "bent," that the penitent (likened to a shofar) must humble himself to reach the highest level for the World to Come. This is why we use a ram's horn, and it is bent, in the manner mentioned shortly.

### And regarding the measure
The penitent, through repentance and by restraining himself, will reach a level of greatness. This is the main point, for those who are perfectly righteous cannot stand in that great place, as mentioned in the Gate of Holiness. Thus, the penitent arrives at such a great level, though one lower than the perfectly righteous. It is already explained in the first Gate that our level is the World to Come and above it, and it is also explained in the third Gate that the level of one penitent is greater and higher in the World to Come than the level of another penitent.

## And this is what is meant by: "In a case of after the fact, all shofars are valid, whether straight or bent."
Meaning, even if it is not from a ram and not bent. By "not from a ram," according to our way, we mean even one who did not repent in his youth when he was in his strength and vigor, which is the superior form of repentance as mentioned above, but waited to repent until his old age, meaning the strength of the vigor of youth and the strength of the "transgression" have passed and gone, meaning that the same transgression, period, place, and woman are not presented before him as before. By "not bent," we mean he does not humble himself to crush his pride, to that difficult level of total humbleness, but has only removed from himself the haughty spirit and the excessive pride that he had previously, which led him to sin, as it is written: "And your heart will be lifted up and you will forget the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 8:14</note>. He now stands on the middle ground of humility, and has not reached the first level, but the level of all evil is removed by repentance, and he has some standing in the World to Come. This is the fifth level mentioned in the third Gate. This is what is meant by "In a case of after the fact, all shofars are valid." This is what our Sages intended in the law of the ram and the bent horn. According to our way, in addition to what we said earlier, you shall prepare the ram's horn so that I may remember for you the Binding of Isaac, and I shall count it for you as if you had bound yourselves before Me, and it is bent so that they may bend their hearts to prayer.

# And they said, "Except for one of a cow, which is invalid in every case."
Its explanation: if it is from a cow, even after the fact, it is invalid. Our Sages hinted here, according to our way, at those people who are like the red heifer that is branded with the redness of sin. If they remain red from transgressions even until old age and hoary hair, they do not return in repentance; or if they do repent, it is out of pride and a haughty spirit, for in every haughty person, pride prevents one from performing repentance, as repentance depends on humility, as mentioned in the sixth Gate. It is said of Ahab, "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before Me?" and so on.

## And this is what is meant by
(And it is not called *shofar* in the Holy Tongue, but *keren* <note>horn</note>.) Since you know that the term *keren* signifies authority, as in "My horn is exalted" <note>1 Samuel 2:1</note>, and "the horn of His anointed," and "the horn of salvation," it means that he has not abandoned pride and authority. Therefore, he does not set his heart to return, as it is written: "And your heart will be lifted up and you will forget the Lord your God," and so on. Therefore, it is invalid, even after the fact, if it is the "horn of pride." For pride does not let him return, as mentioned above. These are those whom our Sages mentioned (in the chapter *Osin Pasin*): the wicked, even at the entrance of Gehenna, do not repent, and they die in their sins because of the horns of their pride.

## And they said, "Because"
And likewise the horns of most animals, meaning the predatory beasts. These are the wicked who are like the wild beasts of the forest, as seen in the chapter *Ha-Mo'il*. They are all one essence, meaning they have no heart of flesh, but a heart of stone and bone, and they harden their hearts from performing repentance all their days, forever, until they die in their sins.

## And this is what is meant by
And they are not bent, meaning they do not remember in the depths of their hearts the day of death, and they are not fearful, not worried, and not saddened by it. Just as our Sages said (in Tractate Shabbat) regarding the verse "There are no bands in their death" <note>Psalms 73:4</note>: The Holy One, blessed be He, said, "It is not enough for the wicked that they are not fearful or saddened by the day of death, but their hearts are healthy to them as an *ulam* <note>vestibule/hall</note>," etc. Therefore, they are completely invalid in the World to Come (just as this shofar is invalid even after the fact). They are the heretics who do not believe in the Day of Judgment, or in the providence over his body and soul to punish, and he is placed among the generations of long ago, as mentioned at the end of the third Gate.

# "All sounds are valid in the shofar"
Meaning the corrections of the sounds. These sounds—meaning even the lightest of all, in the entire Torah—God will count in His mercy, even if there are many sins. A person might say, "What will it avail me to perform this mitzvah if I have committed many sins, and performed many mitzvot?" As it is said, "For with stratagems you shall make your war" <note>Proverbs 24:6</note>, and our Sages interpreted regarding this: a person whose sins have piled up, they shall do against him the sounds.

The Book of Tradition by the <term>Rabad</term> <gloss>Rabbi Abraham ben David</gloss>
until the year 4,849 <note>1089 CE</note>. His servants took him and brought him to Cordoba to be healed, but he passed away there on the Sabbath. His servants took him out of Cordoba and traveled throughout the night until they arrived at Lucena, where he was buried with his ancestors. In addition to his Torah scholarship and his wisdom, he was a great liturgical poet <term>paytan</term> <gloss>poet of liturgical verses</gloss> and knowledgeable in Greek philosophy. He spread much Torah and trained great disciples. Among his greatest disciples was Rabbi Joseph the Judge, Rabbi Jacob ben Sahal, a wise man, a great liturgical poet, and a God-fearing man. He was ordained as a judge in Cordoba in the month of Shevat in the year 4,873 <note>1113 CE</note> and passed away in Nisan in the year 4,884 <note>1124 CE</note>. He judged Israel for eleven years. Among the disciples of Rabbi Isaac bar Rabbi Baruch, the son mentioned previously, was Rabbi Jose bar Rabbi Zaddik ben Zaddik, a wise man, a liturgical poet, and a God-fearing man. He was ordained as a judge in Cordoba in Sivan in the year 4,898 <note>1138 CE</note> and passed away in the year 4,909 <note>1149 CE</note>. He judged Israel for eleven years. He was called a colleague of Rabbi Isaac bar Rabbi Baruch ben Sakhni of the Denia community; sometimes he was called a colleague and sometimes he was called a Rabbi. He was not a colleague to those men, nor did he have the strength in his days to travel from Denia to the land of the <term>Mored</term> <gloss>Rebels/the West</gloss>, yet he was ordained there as a <term>Gaon</term> <gloss>head of a Talmudic academy</gloss> and sat upon the seat of Rav Hai, may his memory be blessed. According to our tradition, we have learned that he did not hold that title or any other in the Talmud throughout all the land of the <unclear>Rebels</unclear>.

The fourth was Rav Isaac bar Rabbi Reuben Al-Bargeloni. He came from Barcelona to the city of Denia. It was a populated place by the sea, and there was a great and holy community there, rich in wealth and good deeds. They honored this Rabbi Isaac, raised him up, and he married into the family of Ibn Al-Khatush, one of the notables of Denia. He sat there and judged them until the day of his death. He was a liturgical poet and composed <term>Azharot</term> <gloss>liturgical poems detailing the commandments</gloss>, and he authored a commentary on chapters of Tractate Ketubot, which testifies to his wisdom and understanding.

Another, greater than them, was Rav Isaac bar Rabbi Jacob ben Alfasi from Qal'at Hammad, a disciple of the Rabbis Nissim bar Jacob and Hananel. He was slandered in his land by Khalfah ben Al-Anab and his son Hayyim until he fled and entered Spain in the year 4,848 <note>1088 CE</note>. Rabbi Joseph the Prince, son of Rabbi Meir ben Shartamiksh, honored and supported him. He entered the city of Cordoba and stayed there for a short time, after which he went to the city of Lucena and remained there until the day of his death. He passed away in Nisan in the year 4,863 <note>1103 CE</note>. He trained many disciples, his fame went out throughout the world, and he composed the <term>Halakhot</term> <gloss>compendium of Jewish law</gloss>, which is like a small Talmud. Since the days of Rav Hai, no one has been found like him in wisdom. These five constitute the second generation. Among the greatest disciples of Rav Isaac bar Rabbi Jacob was Rav Joseph bar Rabbi Meir HaLevi ben Migash, born in the first month of Adar in the year 4,837 <note>1077 CE</note>, and his father Rabbi Meir was a wise disciple.

Just as the letter *alef* and the form, etc., and it is understood that they are included in the soul, they also possessed the aspect that they were in the potential of the soul. It is similar to the analogy of the intellectual faculty and the body of the intellect, the revealed and the revealed—those thoughts act through their intellect, and the thoughts are external vessels, etc. And so it is above; there is also external and internal, as mentioned above in the discourse regarding "and He gave," etc. Through the revelation they are disclosed, and the imprint of the simple throne, etc., until we can speak of the Explicit Name, etc., which all receive. The powers in the soul were more revealed, or at least in a state of concealment, and even though they were not revealed in the external vessels, etc., and the measure and time of the subject of the analogy, etc. And according to the matter of the "grandchild" <note>an allusion to a secondary or derivative state</note>, a person standing on the roof, and it is also more of the essence of the exile, and this is when the house is within the state of exile, and the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>the immanent Divine Presence</gloss> upon it is when the house is within the state of exile, only that there are wicked ones there, and the simple mercy is like the intellectual faculty and the faculties of the soul as they are included in the essence of the soul, like the flame within the coal. 7. One who deposits with his fellow items, whether money or produce, and says to him, "Here is my deposit," and he says to him, "Hide it." If he knew where he placed the deposit—in such-and-such a place he placed the funds—wait for me until I return. And he says to him, "If you [act with] negligence, the loss is upon you," both the assets and the assets of the deposit, and the body of the assets are all meant to be treated the same. And if he was exempt [under the law] to do so and they did not know [what happened], he is exempt from everything.

8. Once he hid it for him, if he was a paid guardian, he is exempt.

9. Once he hid it, but did not guard the key properly, and he left it in an unsafe place and it died [naturally] in its path, he is exempt. If it happened that the beginning was negligence, as you have learned, and <unclear>and so on</unclear> and if it was <term>treifah</term> <gloss>terminally ill/torn animal</gloss>, and if he did not... <unclear>then he was liable</unclear>. But if he did not <unclear>hide it</unclear> <unclear>properly</unclear> and it died in its path, like the case of the <term>negev</term> <gloss>south/desert</gloss>, behold, he hid it, he is liable, for he was a paid guardian who did not [act as required]. If it died, behold, he had the status of one who acted against the <term>negev</term> and his placement caused it to die. And likewise for any similar case.

10. If the depositor raised the <unclear>assets</unclear> <unclear>and the negev</unclear> <gloss>desert/south</gloss>, they are, behold, this is negligence. If it died naturally, he is exempt.

11. If he asked for a concession to be exempted, and he exempted him, he is exempt against his will. This is similar to <unclear>placing</unclear>, and a paid guardian is exempt.

12. A paid guardian who left the animal and entered a house and it died <unclear>in the heat</unclear> and it was trampled, if it was torn and he entered in error, if he had a way for people to enter into <unclear>a place of pity</unclear>, he would not be able to save it, if he was there, he is liable. And if he <unclear>could not</unclear>, he is exempt.

13. The way of deposits: The deposit has a way of being hidden, like grain and like beams and timber, and there is a deposit whose way of being hidden is to place it in a barn, like bedding and cloaks, and there is a deposit whose way of being hidden is to place it in a chest or a box and lock it, like coins and jewelry, and so on.

14. One who hid the deposit in a place whose method of protection is fitting for it, and it was stolen from there, even if he did not hide it with the [same level of care] as he would his own, if the house was breached and it was torn, behold, this is negligence and he is liable to pay. Even though he placed the deposit with his own, if it was fitting to be hidden well, and if the place was fitting to be hidden, he is liable as if he did not... <unclear>for he did not</unclear> guard it.

15. Funds, coins, golden vessels, and good silver, the way of hiding them is to dig in the ground and put over them a handbreadth of earth. If he hid it in the foundation of the wall, in the lowest part adjacent to the ground, or adjacent to the beam, even if he did not put it in the ground, as long as he put a handbreadth in the depth... if he did not hide it in the wall of the wall, the assets might be scattered and lost. If he locked them appropriately in a chest or hid them in a place where people do not recognize and do not wander, it is a fortiori that he is negligent and liable to pay.

16. One who deposits with his fellow coins near the time of the seasons, he is liable to pay and to guard them until the end of the year. If he said "until the end of the year," and he did not watch, and they were entered [into the house] under duress, he is liable. And if he was a student, if the depositor knew, he is liable until he returns them to his fellow <unclear>to the</unclear> ground.

17. If the depositary stipulated on condition that he would not hide it in the ground, and likewise all matters, we follow his condition.

18. In a place where funds have a method of being hidden other than in the ground, such as <unclear>money boxes</unclear> and many places that are hidden <unclear>elsewhere</unclear>, in a place where it is customary to hide them in the ground, but he places them in a place where he places his own coins, he is exempt.

19. Even if he did not hide them in the ground, they did not say funds must be hidden in the ground, except when the depositor was silent. But if he said to his fellow to hide them, he is exempt unless he said to him, "You deal with them and gain profit," for that is as if he said to him explicitly to place the capital in the ground.

20. One who deposited coins with his fellow in a way to bring them to his house, or with him to the streets, and they are taken by his hand, or he binds them as is fitting until he arrives, and he buries them as is fitting. And if he did not do so in the way of carrying, even in a case of duress, he is liable to pay, for he acted with negligence.

21. Anyone who deposits <unclear>an item</unclear>, whether vessels or coins, on the knowledge that the older children would deposit it, [if the depositary returned the deposit to the children, he is exempt].

<header>Yotzer for Parashat Shekalim</header>

**Blessed** are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who forms light and creates darkness, makes peace, and creates all things. Eternal light in the treasury of life, lights from darkness, He spoke and it was.
God, who is exalted above all to the summit, chose a nation <note>Israel</note> humble of head. Like a firstborn among figs at the start <note>alluding to the first fruits</note>, He beckoned to God and sought it out, to set it apart from all nations, to lift it above every head. He shall cause the despised to dwell in the dread of the head, and it shall raise its head upon the throne of glory from the beginning.
My redeemer and the lifter of my head, now He shall pass over my head, and seek and inquire, Holy.
He spoke in this book, and confirmed with eloquent words, for those who are likened to dust and ashes, that they should give a ransom, without blemish or shame, to atone for their iniquity, and their righteousness shall be written in a book.
In the remembrance of the book, for their unleavened bread <note>a reference to the offering</note>, together with me who am dust and ashes. This is our God, the seer of my father, and they showed him a form of a coin of fire in a vision. And all shall prophesy of this; He will extend loving-kindness in this. And after them, where shall they build, and Judah shall gather them, and they shall sit in goodness upon this. And they shall be able to see the Divine Presence, and a nation shall trample nation, He shall act. The Unique One, who dwells on high, graced her with the perfect Torah, for the dove that is pure. Whoever passes by, let them weigh a shekel without confusion; the half-shekel is a contribution for their benefit, without comparison, and it shall be a wall for her, He who suspends the earth over nothingness. From twenty years old they shall volunteer with song, the face of Him who dwells in the habitation, princes and ways with support. All shall be equal in giving, without delay, Selah, and round about supplication, at all times and at every season. And they shall endure with song, a ransom for their souls, and their sin He shall redeem, and goodness shall be distributed. They shall improve, Aram shall recount all, and praise they shall tell and complete, and thanksgiving to the Rock they shall sing. Their rocks shall be diminished and straightened, and upon their necks they shall prevail, and in abundance of joy they shall be blessed.
Their congregation to be strengthened in the Torah, without any more to the curse, when they sacrificed this to idolatry. With them He appointed in love and desire, in salvation and establishment, their name in life always. In all the completion of praise, for me without service, it shall always be for a memorial to the Rose of Sharon, in atonement and advantage, before the High One, Holy. All shall thank You.
You loved Your people for the sake of the generations from on high. You magnified Your name for them, You caused them to cleave to the love of Your name. They are Your inheritance and Your people, and they are persistent in exalting You, and He shall remember the covenant of Him who speaks to You. Have pity and bring near to them Your day. Goodness You gave to the mighty, they weighed silver as atonements, a ransom for iniquity they make atonement. Forever they shall be preserved, from the age of the commandment of twenty, the giving of the poor and the rich, the handful of all that is counted, upon their banner in all directions. They have accounted and their names.

<header>Yotzer for the Second Sabbath of Hanukkah</header>

Among the people and the spirits, the sons were victorious, and the army went out in their flesh as though refreshed. And they heard the voice of the Lord God. The illness of the assembly, a peg fixed to humble and to storm, Ekron was uprooted, Caesarea the daughter marched; therefore from the beginning of the year. Who among us brought tidings, in the name of the Lord my banner, circles of a name, one is called the Tower of the Prince. And it lived like a leader in Judah, and Ekron as a foundation. In fear, Tyre and Sidon and the cities of their generations shall dwell before Him in many, and they learned their Torah, in their courtyards and their castles. Those who were far off acted in their years as they pleased, as the rule of masters. They ruled over their bodies, and service, and affliction, knowledge, and disputes. And the building of Elishah and Tarshish, Kittim and Dodanim. From passing over, Greeks were sold to the sons of Greeks, one hundred and eighty years, in the rushing of silver to prostrate themselves, and they seized the oils. They gave to the treasury of the king gold darics. Friendship of the kingdom of priests, and the beauty of the holy that is honored, that in its time was tripled, and for them was the sending of every meal offering. And in it the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer a gift. From fifty they rescued fifty, until the feast of peace, the army of the war, in which on the twenty-fifth of Kislev, they went to their tents rejoicing and good of heart. All the stones of the altar that the Greeks had defiled, they gathered and hid in the northeast for the sake of mercy. And they took other stones and brought them to under the stones. The Unique One, for the day they gathered for song and for praise, the upright ministers in light to offer and to sacrifice their offering for the dedication of the altar. They willed the one greater than his brothers, and he was grasping with the longing of slaughter, like the act of an angel, the hands of every banner his hand, bread and wine, and he was like one girded on high. A host of horsemen came to profane the House of the Forest. A lattice host was ten in measurement. They broke through and passed the gate. Friends like the strength of thirteen in the gap in the city, therefore they ordained for their number bowings for the month, and they bowed to the Lord in the splendor of holiness. The enemy and his army, at the time they were wiped out, the runners went out to bring tidings in the borders, salvation blossomed, to bring Jerusalem to celebrate Hanukkah with joy. They dedicated the honor of the palace to kindle a lamp with skill, as they searched and found in the depths, and a flask that was hidden to be set aside, for it was only a cruse of oil. And they returned and found in it for eight days, they established to tell, and they established therefore these days for generations forever, to remind of the mighty deeds, and to give thanks and to praise to the Lord, from your womb, and they wore righteousness in your enclosure, His name and His sign. Divide the secret and sing in your paths, olive oil. A Psalm of the song of the dedication of the House, for David.
All shall thank You

## Liturgy for Parashat Shekalim

**Blessed** are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who forms light and creates darkness, makes peace and creates everything. The light of the world in the treasury of life, lights from darkness, He spoke and it was.
God, exalted above all, at the head. He chose a nation, humble of head. Like the first-ripe fruit on the tree, at the head. He sought it, and requested it. To set it apart from all nations. To exalt it above every head. He shall appoint the redeemed to be a terror to the head. And it shall lift its head. On the throne of glory from the beginning.
My redeemer and lifter of my head. Now it shall pass over my head. And he shall seek and search, Holy.
He spoke in this book. And fulfilled it in fair sayings. For those likened to dust and ashes. That they should give a ransom. Without blemish or shame. To atone for their iniquity. And their righteousness shall be written in a book.
In the memory of the book. For their merits, along with I also am dust and ashes. This was shown to our father as a vision. And they showed him a kind of coin of fire in the vision. And also everything shall be prophesied in this. He will place kindness in this. And after them, where shall they build and bind them, Judah, and well shall they sit upon this. And the Divine Presence <note>original: "שכינה" (Shekhinah)</note> they shall be able to behold. And a nation trampled upon nations, he shall stir. The Unique One, dwelling on high. He favored her with the perfect Torah. To the dove who is pure. Whoever passes through whatever. They shall weigh a shekel without turmoil. A half-shekel as a contribution. For their benefit without measure. And it shall be a wall for her. Who hangs the earth on nothing. From twenty years old they shall volunteer with song. The face of the Dweller of the dwelling. Princes and ways with a staff. All shall be equal in the giving. Without further delay, Selah, and surroundings of supplication. At every time and every season. And they shall be established with song. Upon their souls atonement, and their sin they shall redeem, and good shall be distributed. They shall improve, the Arameans shall all recount. And praise they shall tell and complete. And thanksgiving to the Rock they shall sing. Their rocks shall be diminished and straightened, and upon their necks they shall prevail. And in the abundance of joys they shall be blessed.
Their congregation, to strengthen themselves in the Torah. Without further curse. By their drawing near this to idolatry. With them He appointed in love and desire. In salvation and in establishment. Their name in the life which is constant. In every totality of praise, and to me, without labor, always it shall be a remembrance to the Rose of Sharon. In atonement and excellence. Before the High One. Holy. All shall praise You.
You loved Your people because of generation after generation from on high. You magnified Your name for them. You caused them to cleave to the love of Your name. They are Your inheritance and Your people. And they are constant in exalting You, and He shall remember the covenant of Your speaker. Have pity and bring near to them Your day. Goodness You gave to the mighty ones. They weighed silver for atonements. A ransom for iniquity, atoning. Forever they shall be preserved. From the age of the commandment, twenty. The giving of the poor and the rich. The handful of all that are counted. Upon their sign in all boundaries. They accounted them and their names.

## Liturgy for the Second Sabbath of Hanukkah

Among the people and the spirits. The sons were victorious, and the army went out in their flesh as though refreshed. And they heard the voice of the Lord God. The illness of the dwelling, a peg stuck fast, to diminish and to stir. Let Ekron be uprooted, the daughter of the step, therefore from the beginning of the year. Who in news have we reaped, in the name of the Lord my banner. Assemblies of the name, one is called the tower of the prince. And living like a chieftain in Judah, and Ekron, a washing. In trembling, Tyre and Sidon and the cities of their generations, in many they shall dwell before Him and learn His Torah. In their courtyards and their castles. The distant ones acted in their years according to their will as the law of masters. They ruled over their bodies, and service and labor, acquaintances and disputes. And the building of Elisha and Tarshish, Kittim and Dodanim. From passing, the Greeks were sold to the sons of the Greeks. One hundred and eighty years. In the desire for silver to grovel, and the oil was seized. They gave to the king's treasury golden darics. The friendship of the kingdom of priests and the glory of the holy, the honored. That in its time was sent, and to them was the sending of every meal offering, and in it the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer a gift. From fifty they liberated fifty, until the feast of peace, the army of the war, which was on the twenty-fifth of Kislev. And they went to their tents rejoicing and good of heart. All the stones of the altar that the Greeks had defiled. They gathered them and hid them in the northeast of the dwelling of grace. And they took other stones and brought them to under the stones. The Unique One, for the day they gathered for song and for praise. The upright ones serving in light to offer and to sacrifice. Their offering for the dedication of the altar. He desired the one greater than his brothers, and he was taking a handful in the desire of slaughter, as the work of an angel, the hands of every banner his hand, bread and wine, and he is as one who strips the exalted. A force of horsemen came to profane the House of the Forest. The interlacing force was ten cubits in height. They breached and passed the gate. Friends, as the strength of thirteen in the break in the fence. Therefore they ordained for their number bowings for the month. And they bowed to the Lord in the beauty of holiness. The enemy and his army, at the time when they were wiped out. The runners went out to herald in the borders, salvation has blossomed. To bring Jerusalem to make a Hanukkah with joy. They dedicated the glory of the temple to raise a lamp with skill. As they sought and found in the pit and the surrounding that was hidden to prepare. For only a flask of oil. And they returned and found in it for eight days, they established to recount, and they established therefore these days for generations forever, to remind of the mighty deeds and to thank and to praise to the Lord, from Your belly, and they shall wear righteousness in Your protection, His name and His sign. Divide the secret and sing in your paths, olive oil. A psalm, a song for the dedication of the house, by David.
All shall praise You

He must endure that <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>loving-kindness</gloss> may be wrought for the sake of the worlds, and to speak of their mystery.

For this, our Sages took care regarding her oath, an oath in the book of Baba Kamma <note>original: "בב'ק'ח'" (a reference to the Talmudic tractate Baba Kamma)</note> concerning every place, blessed be He, and concerning every curse, and concerning all that is in the vows in His Great Name, with the obligation of the entire Torah, and upon them and their Torah, that His kindness shall return to him from the honor of her turning, not with silver, and not with silver, and not according to His mercies to the one who strengthens his property. What have you seen and what have you heard from us, and what greatness it is to forgive one who has sinned. Furthermore, one must know what this "grace" <term>chesed</term> <gloss>loving-kindness/grace</gloss> means, for you have known that your fear <note>i.e., awe/reverence for God</note> shall be upon them. Because you forgive those who have sinned, they will fear you and be afraid lest they sin against you, lest you punish them according to their sins instead of forgiving them upon seeing their repentance. This grace will return, especially in this forgiveness regarding the sin of the Golden Calf, where He forgave them but punished them little by little. This is the meaning of "visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children," as Rashi explains on the verse "visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children." Similarly, in Psalm 103, regarding the verse "For with You is the forgiveness, that You may be feared." For according to the strict justice and judgment of the Lord, there should be punishment, but through pardon and forgiveness, the doubt in the sinner’s mind is strengthened—perhaps by repentance the Holy One, blessed be He, will forgive him. Through this, he is strengthened to return in repentance and fears lest he return to his folly, and he fears sin. From this, he is awakened; for when the wicked see mercy upon seeing their repentance, they see within themselves that their transgressions are great and that they have sinned against the great and awesome Name. Through this, they fear the Name of the Lord, may He be exalted, because of their sin at the time they perform repentance. Through the forgiveness granted to them on account of their fear, grace returns to them if they persist in their fear, and this is "the grace of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear Him."

The explanation of "from everlasting to everlasting" is according to its measure, according to the thirteen attributes by which the world was created. Therefore, they are in forgiveness after their sin, not in a general way but specifically, according to their repentance and their fear, so that they may see the greatness of the Lord’s power, the greatness of His stature, His goodness, and His grace. The explanation is: instead of the matter for which they sinned, and regarding the subject of "and His righteousness unto children's children," the meaning is: through the grace of the Lord, He visits their sins upon them with forgiveness and grace, as Rashi explains in the portion *Ki Tisa*. And "His righteousness" means the grace that He distributed to them, for it was as an act of charity <term>tzedakah</term> <gloss>righteousness/charity</gloss> that He dealt with them, for He had mercy upon them. This grace will return to them, for He visits their iniquities upon them little by little, because you have known to pass over them with graces and forgiveness. They will fear the Lord in the forgiveness; for when they see this constantly, they will fear the Lord. This is the grace of the Lord, for it will return to them from everlasting to everlasting, and this is the grace of the Lord and His righteousness unto children's children, so that they may endure the iniquities of their fathers. This is what the Scripture says: "And the grace of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting."

At the end of the first chapter of *Rosh Hashanah*, Rav Judah said: A covenant is made for the thirteen attributes that they shall not return empty, as it is written, "Behold, I make a covenant," etc. It is necessary to know what grace is here in this covenant. When they see that the grace of the Lord and His righteousness are unto children's children, He visits their iniquities upon them, and this is a "covenant made." This covenant and grace are through the thirteen attributes by which the world was created. The Lord created the world with grace and with the attribute of mercy, and through these thirteen attributes, mercy and grace are awakened, just as they were at the creation, "In the beginning God created," etc. Through these thirteen attributes, the grace of the Lord is awakened "from everlasting to everlasting," and "His righteousness unto children's children." His righteousness and His grace will return to them through the merit of the fathers and through the thirteen attributes by which the world was created, and this is "and the grace of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting."

# Chapter 5, Part of the Purpose, Chapter 8

For it has already been explained at the end of the introduction to this book that the portion imposed [upon the righteous] and its branches are in proportion to the upper wings, and as this was also explained at the beginning of Chapter 17-18 of the first part of this book, regarding what was mentioned there concerning the conditions and rectification of the service intended in the Upper Realm. It also includes all the decrees, properties, and measurements, as was explained there. There is much agreement and consistency in this regarding the other discourses on the rectification and importance of all the limbs, in the secret of the structure and in the value of the soul in every table, in its creation and its fall. And so, all the languages and the movement written in every <term>Ma'aseh Bereshit</term> <gloss>Account of Creation</gloss>, as we wrote in Chapter 20 of the second part of this book at the end. Its secret is that I will return to the secret of the beginning and the firmament, and like the matter of "Let there be light," "Let there be a firmament," "Let there be lights," our Father in the light, "And let there be light for a living soul," our Father in a language deep in the <term>Ma'aseh Bereshit</term>, in the firmament, in the matter, and in the living creatures of the earth, and our Father in the essence of the Name. Our Father in the language of <term>Beriah</term> <gloss>Creation</gloss>, as in the <term>Ma'aseh Bereshit</term> and in the light, "And God called the light," in His revelation, our Father as living creatures, and elevating it above all—in all of this, the language of <term>Yetzirah</term> <gloss>Formation</gloss> was not mentioned. However, in the saying "And the Lord God formed <note>Hebrew: *vayyitzer*</note> man," and what is written "And out of the ground the Lord God formed every beast of the field," they already said in <term>Bereshit Rabbah</term> 17 that it means to subdue and to overcome well from the material. "Formed" (<term>yetzirah</term>) is a language of subduing. The reason seems to be that the entire <term>Ma'aseh Bereshit</term> is prepared and moves according to these souls, which are like the work of the covenant, "if not for My covenant by day and night," etc. And they fear Him, He who found the sea and established the earth, in His shaping, He mimics worlds and draws in its proportion, and good deeds are its initial light. For in its depth, always in the sons, God acquires Torah, and teaches in every law, if he adds and renews in the work of the Torah and its attributes. And the foundation in it is the language of formation (<term>yetzirah</term>) to reveal its husband, as they recognized in the <term>Midrash</term> of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai <note>Rashbi</note> regarding what is written: "Everyone that is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory, I have formed him, yes, I have made him." For the supernal Glory has in it the covenant of formation and making. However, it was created for the rectification of the Glory, and for this reason, these languages are included in it, as was explained in Chapter 17 of the first part of this book. In the name of the thousand oaks among all the created beings, who understand the purpose? Therefore, it did not come in the name of the language of formation. All this <unclear>certain person R. Wise</unclear> to teach him in what he said, that he is this, etc., to equate him to the rest of the created beings in that he is without determination. And with you, so too will they say not in it, and the time of success to add in the degree of the righteous and chosen, for all created beings are their vessels and they rectify worlds, they are drawn to him. For according to Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Abba, we can say that the created beings are in the value of the righteous, as the servants to the King, for they are the ones who prepare the actions for the King, like the ministers who were tasked to serve them in His kingship, His rule, and His dominion. And it is fitting to consider that the nations in all this are lacking much of the levels of the Torah, and this is to show that all created beings are in a state of being drawn to the righteous, even in the rectification of his food and drink, as is known regarding the levels of the righteous and the generations in the honor of the <term>Sefirot</term> <gloss>divine emanations</gloss> and the connections. And it is written of them: "And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth," in the verse that is written in the words of the <term>Ramban</term> <note>Nachmanides</note>, of blessed memory, who wrote in Chapter 23 of this, at the end, the language, and he said: "And furthermore, they said concerning the stars, 'to give light upon the void,' and from this was written its reasons, in order to enjoy that which is joined, that which is clarified," meaning the lights from the pearls, as it is said regarding man: "And have dominion over the fish of the sea." Its meaning is that it was not spoken for that, only to return to our faces, that the intent is about him with the revelation in order to say that all created beings came for the sake of the righteous and his benefit and his assistance. And what is written "to give light," etc., all is to give light, a claim to strengthen the claim that he is intended in the world, to act for the good of the world, until they are in their essence with taste and understanding, that the faith is for that, meaning to be man. And so wrote the Sages <note>Chazal</note> and added more in the book of the <term>Kuzari</term>. And this is what he said: "The entire world was not created but to serve this." In this connection it is explained, and his creation is for that, and he blessed them without counting all <column-break/>

that which is deficiency and rectification for his existence, so that he may be always free and ready for the supernal life and the rectification of the Glory; this matter was the goal of his purpose. And the Sages have already said in the <term>Sifrei</term> that the upper beings were created to serve the lower beings. These are indeed the words of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish: "The ball of the heel of the first man obscured the globe of the sun." And do not wonder at this: a star in the world does a favor for the inhabitants. He said to him: And as for you, in the service of whom does it do good? It is for you. So too, the first man was created for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the globe of the sun for the service of the creatures, except that the ball of the heel of the first man would obscure the globe of the sun. And he who has a face will see that the righteous are not intended for themselves, for all actions, since they were not born for themselves; so too, all created beings did not come intended for themselves, for they came for Him as well. And you, all created beings, are a symbol of the light and the man to serve his Creator, as he taught at the end of <term>Kiddushin</term>: "I was created to serve my Creator." And the saying that the globe of the sun is for the service of creatures is evidence that it is not according to the words of the Master who said that they are intended for themselves, and it is in his ability that they are the law of this and the <term>Sefirot</term> until it is elevated. And explicitly, the Sages said that the upper beings were created for the honor of the lower beings. It is written to give reasons after the Holy One, blessed be He, to the owner, but he says to the Congregation of Israel, it is written: "The constellations I have created in My world," and can it be that I have created them for Israel? And in <term>Bereshit Rabbah</term> at the beginning of "Open the tent," for a good deed you opened for the creatures, and for a good deed you opened for the righteous: "If not for My covenant, I would not have created heaven and earth, etc." And he is astonished concerning the creatures of the world, if I did not create the globe of the sun, as it is written: "He set a tent in them." "Creatures, if I did not create the Torah, as it is written: 'If not for My covenant [I would not have created] day and night...'" And the Sages say this to demonstrate that this is the gate.

Those believers who sit at home, except for those with a disability, are not equal to those who strive in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives. God has given higher rank to those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home. To each, God has promised the best reward, but He has favored those who strive over those who stay behind with a great reward: degrees of status from Him, as well as forgiveness and mercy. God is ever forgiving and merciful. As for those whom the angels take in death while they have wronged themselves, the angels will ask, "What was your situation?" They will reply, "We were oppressed in the land." The angels will say, "Was not God's earth spacious enough for you to migrate within it?" Their abode will be Hell, an evil destination. Except for the truly oppressed among the men, women, and children who have no means and cannot find a way out. It is these whom God may pardon, for God is ever pardoning and forgiving. Whoever migrates in the cause of God will find in the earth many places of refuge and abundance. Whoever leaves his home migrating toward God and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him, his reward is surely incumbent upon God. God is ever forgiving and merciful. When you travel in the land, there is no

<column-break/>

sin upon you if you shorten the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may attack you, for the disbelievers are your clear enemies. When you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you, and let them take their weapons. When they have prostrated, let them be behind you, and let another group that has not yet prayed come forward and pray with you, and let them take their precautions and their weapons. Those who disbelieve wish that you were heedless of your weapons and your luggage so that they could swoop down upon you all at once. There is no sin upon you if you lay aside your weapons if you are troubled by rain or are ill, provided you take your precautions. God has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment. When you have completed the prayer, remember God while standing, sitting, or on your sides. When you are secure again, perform the prayer fully, for the prayer has been prescribed for the believers at fixed times. Do not be weak in pursuing the enemy. If you are suffering, they are also suffering as you are suffering, but you hope for from God what they do not hope for. God is ever knowing and wise. We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so that you may judge between people by what God has shown you.

Those of the believers who remain at home, other than those disabled, and those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives, are not equal. Allah has ranked those who strive with their wealth and their lives higher than those who remain at home. To each, Allah has promised the best reward, but Allah has distinguished those who strive over those who remain at home with a great reward: degrees of rank from Him, forgiveness, and mercy. Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful. Indeed, as for those whom the angels take in death while they were wronging themselves, the angels will ask, "In what condition were you?" They will reply, "We were oppressed in the land." The angels will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious enough for you to emigrate within it?" For such people, their refuge is Hell, and it is an evil destination. Except for the oppressed among men, women, and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they guided to a way. Perhaps Allah will pardon them, for Allah is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving. Whoever emigrates for the cause of Allah will find on the earth many locations and abundance. After the death of Mūsā bin Shākir, al-Ma'mūn, who cared for the Banū Mūsā brothers, entrusted Isḥāk bin Ibrāhīm with their guardianship. Thus, the Mūsā brothers during their education had the possibility to study deeply into the subjects for which they had talent and interest.

The life of the Banū Mūsā brothers was as simple as that of Ma'mūn's close circle brought from Marw to Baghdad in 813. But, soon after the death of al-Ma'mūn, their lives became luxurious. The wealth and influence of the brothers developed through the favors of the caliphs and the income sources credited to their names. They devoted much of their wealth to the quest for the works of ancient writers, sent missions to Byzantium to seek out such material, paid a group of translators to render them into Arabic, and spent great energy on the development of the sciences. This attitude served as a model for others, such as Qusta bin Lūqā. Muḥammed is said to have made a journey to Anatolia for this reason and brought back with him, from Harran to Baghdad, one of the most famous scientists and a renowned translator of Islam, Thābit bin Qurrā. The brothers used to pay about five hundred dinars a month to a group of translators who worked on the collected texts in the House of Wisdom.

The brothers' interest and ability in geometry, ingenious devices, music, and astronomy were not always of the same level. Among them, Abu Ja'far Muḥammed was the most influential; it is said that he knew the works of Euclid and Ptolemy, and that his knowledge in the fields of mathematics, astronomy, logic, and philosophy was extensive. Aḥmed's talent was in technical matters. The books on the construction of ingenious devices (<term>hiyal</term>) <gloss>mechanical devices/ruses</gloss> and musical automation must be his work. Ḥasan was a brilliant geometrician. Muḥammed was also highly active in politics. They lived mostly together, remained active during the reigns of various caliphs, and were sociable in the modern sense.

Knowledge is either <term>tasawwur</term> <gloss>conceptualization</gloss>, the way to which is through definition, or <term>tasdiq</term> <gloss>assent/propositional knowledge</gloss>, the way to which is through <term>burhan</term> <gloss>demonstration</gloss>. There is nothing in this that should be denied. It is of the same category as what the <term>Mutakallimun</term> <gloss>theologians</gloss> and scholars of dialectic have mentioned regarding proofs. They only differ in terminology and jargon, and in the greater detail they apply to definitions and subdivisions. An example of their discourse is their statement: If it is established that all A are B, then it follows that some B are A. That is, if it is established that every human is an animal, it follows that some animal is a human. They express this by saying that a universal affirmative proposition converts into a particular affirmative proposition. What relation does this have to the essential matters of religion that it should be rejected and denied? If it is denied, the only result from the perspective of logicians is a poor opinion of the intellect of the denier, and indeed of the religion that he claims depends upon such a denial. Yes, they do commit a type of wrong in this science, which is that they gather conditions for demonstration that they know will inevitably produce certainty, but when they arrive at religious aims, they are unable to fulfill those conditions and instead become extremely lax. Sometimes someone who studies logic also finds it appealing and clear, so he assumes that the infidelities reported of the philosophers are supported by such proofs, and he rushes into disbelief before reaching the divine sciences.

This corruption also infects it.

### 3 - As for the natural sciences:
It is an investigation into the realm of the heavens, its stars, and what lies beneath them among the simple bodies such as water, air, earth, and fire; and into composite bodies such as animals, plants, and minerals; and into the causes of their transformation, change, and mixture. Just as it is not a condition of religion to deny the science of medicine, it is also not a condition of religion to deny that science, except in specific issues that we have mentioned in the book <italic>The Incoherence of the Philosophers</italic>. Their various tastes, for all of that is a dragging of the imagination. Likewise, the form which is said to be "He," and that all things are parts of its essence. Likewise, the One which appears as if it were an accident to essence, and resembles existence. And that the Necessary <note>a reference to the Necessary Being, <term>al-wajib al-wujud</term></note> is this, while others are like the prior essence. It may be imagined that it is the Possible, and that other than this existence, or that which has existence, has an aspect of its own essence, which is pure need, and an aspect toward this existence, by which it is existent. Neither the monotheism of the Garden, nor the monotheism of its people, nor the monotheism of him who said: "The threshold of the Truth is too majestic to be a thoroughfare for every comer." Nor the monotheism of him who said: "No one has unified the One." Nor the monotheism of him who said: "He is not seen except by His light, and not witnessed except by His presence." Nor he who said: "How can He who is the means of seeing be seen?" In sum, the One <note>referencing the classification of unity in Aristotle's Metaphysics</note> is limited to four kinds: the one by continuity, the one as a whole and a completion, the first simple one in each genus, and the universal one predicated with priority and posteriority on all that is enumerated in metaphysics. All of this offers no liberation, nor is it pure in terms of the perfection that contains all three perfections: I mean the perfection that cuts through the imagination, verifies the Truth, and to which all things respond—not in the way mentioned, and it is possible, for its essence moves and it moves with it, and its bliss is likewise intended. It resembles the magnet, in which a cycle is required for those who understand and have analyzed these words and then redirected them. This knowledge is in the mind before conception and assent, not after them. The ignorant sage is he who says: Life is a condition for intellect, intellect is a condition for knowledge, knowledge is a condition for action, action is a condition for virtue, virtue is a condition for happiness, happiness is a condition for goodness, goodness is a condition for perfection, perfection is a condition for unity, and unity is the condition for the sought-after goal. The sought-after goal is that which is spoken of in synonymy with things, and in homonymy before them, and in shared participation after them, and in weighting with them in relation to it, and in derivation within them, and in passing away from them through it, and in metaphor within them for it.

The virtuous, knowledgeable person places the condition in the place of the conditioned, and the wise successor makes the condition the conditioned without priority or delay. The wise and knowing one does not find that, for he is that.

Nor the monotheism of one who said: "He is only seen by His light, and He is only witnessed by His presence." Nor of one who said: "How can He be seen when it is through Him that one sees?" In short, the One [451] is confined to four kinds: the one by continuity, the one in terms of being a whole and a completion, the first simple one in every genus, and the universal one predicated with priority and posteriority upon all that is enumerated in metaphysics. All of this offers no salvation, nor is there anything pure therein in terms of the perfection that contains all three perfections—I mean the perfection that cuts through the imagination, verifies the Truth, and to which all respond, though not in the manner mentioned. It is possible, and its essence moves, and it moves along with it, and its bliss is likewise intended. It is likened to a magnet, in which the cycle is necessary for those who understand and weigh these words, then divert them. This knowledge exists in the eternal mind before conception and assent, not after them. The wise ignorant person is the one who says: "Life is a condition for intellect, intellect is a condition for knowledge, knowledge is a condition for action, action is a condition for virtue, virtue is a condition for happiness, happiness is a condition for goodness, goodness is a condition for perfection, perfection is a condition for unity, and unity is a condition for the Desired Object." The Desired Object is that which is spoken of synonymously with things, univocally before them, by participation after them, by preference with them for its sake, by derivation within them, by removal from it, and by metaphor within them for it.

He named them by their names, arranged the actions, and assigned to each of them their proper station according to your understanding. Compose from them whatever action, remembrance, or exercise you wish, and use it to connect his world with your own world. From this, a purity is gathered, and you shall see from the traces of God Almighty’s craftsmanship that which tires the mind’s eye to perceive.

The most virtuous night of the year is **the Night of Power** <note>Laylat al-Qadr, the night the Quran was first revealed.</note>, and the most virtuous of its days is **the Day of Arafah**. The proportion of the Night of Power to the year is like the proportion of the soul to the body, and the proportion of the Day of Arafah is like the proportion of the intellect. The year is composed of minutes, degrees, hours, days, and months, just as the human is composed from the zygote <note>nutfa</note>, to the clot <note>alaqa</note>, to the lump of flesh <note>mudgha</note>, to the bones, to the flesh, to the formation, and to the breath of life. Understand this, for I have opened for you a noble and simple door to the wonders of composition in the two existences <note>the macrocosm and the microcosm</note>. This flash of insight is most fitting for this abridgment, so draw analogies from it. If the first day of the noble month of Ramadan is a Sunday, then watch for the blessed night during the odd-numbered nights of the first ten days. If it is Monday night...

<meta>catchword: in</meta>

---

...then it is in the middle ten days. If it is Tuesday night, then it is in the last ten days, in its odd-numbered nights. Wednesday, Thursday, and up to the end of Friday are composed based on Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday, like the increase of the fourth over the third in the field of numbers. Since Tuesday combines the even and the odd <note>al-shaf wa al-witr</note> and is the limit of number <gloss>and its regulator</gloss>, it follows the days of the week in the subsequent tens. I hold that the Night of Power rotates within the month. The external cause occurs in ten ways: it happens either from excessive heat, or from a cold complexion obstructing the ear, or from hot water in a bath, or from cold water while swimming in it, or from some reptiles entering the ear, or from some other thing like hair, grains, or seeds, or from a puncture by a needle or wood causing a wound in the place called <term>alfomach</term> <gloss>the ear canal</gloss>, or from the entry of hot substances that cause harm like processed <term>euphorbium</term> <gloss>a caustic resin</gloss> and laurel berries and the like, or from a blow or concussion affecting the ear. The sign of a plethora of blood is redness of the face, heaviness of the head and forehead when leaning forward, and intensity of throbbing; if the age, complexion, and season agree with this, it will be stronger. The sign of a hot humor is intense heat and inflammation of the ear and the patient's delight in cool air; when the age, complexion, and season agree with this, it will be more severe. The sign of thick gas is a pulling or stretching sensation and much noise in the ear with lightness of the head. The sign of a pustule or abscess, which is called <term>almelas</term> <gloss>abscess</gloss>, is intense pain which is called <term>almelas</term>, and it is the strongest of all ear pains and more dangerous, accompanied by pain in the whole forehead, head, and fever. The signs of obstruction from blood collected in the ear are heaviness of hearing and mildness of pain, and that you should place the patient in the sun until the sight of the eye falls upon it. The signs of the cause of tooth eruption in children are that the eruption is manifest and there is diarrhea. The signs of cold or heat and vapor offending the ear from the outside are those the patient reports, and because it happens after repetition. The sign of hot water entering the ear is that they entered a bath and that they feel the water. The sign of cold water is that they swam in it and they feel the water when the head is moved. The sign of animals entering the ear is that sometimes they move and sometimes they do not, and it is with noise and pain when the animal moves. The sign of the cause of that animal or stone or any other foreign object entering is that it appears to the sense and touch from what the patient relates. The sign of the cause of some hot or cold medicine is from what the patient reports feeling of heat or cold; they feel cold with heaviness of movement and do not feel pain. The sign from a blow or concussion is that it is visible to the eye and is grasped by the feeling of the impact. Its treatment, when it is from a cause of blood, is that the cephalic vein should be bled, and the diet should be restricted, especially from meats

When it is from a cold humor, the body should be loosened with <term>cochia</term> pills <gloss>a type of purgative pill</gloss> and <term>yera</term> <gloss>hieras/laxative medicine</gloss>, the diet should be thinned, and there should be instilled into the ear oil of costus or spike oil and other similar oils, and the ear should be plastered with warm bran. When it occurs from thick gas, there should first be evacuation and the head should be cleansed, and there should be instilled into the ear oil of rue or oil of castor and euphorbium, and the ear should be plastered with cooked and warm calamint, dill, and chamomile. Its treatment in children is that they should rub their gums so their eruption is accelerated, and among those things for them is hen fat, woman's milk, the blood of doves, and similar things. When it happens from cold or heat or wind as has been said, the heat should be cooled and the cold warmed with a plaster or ointment. When it happens with hot or cold medicine, each of them should be cured with its opposite, as has been said in the preceding. When it is from a blow or concussion, frankincense should be ground and mixed with woman's milk and instilled into the ear.

Regarding noise and ringing of the ears follows. Chapter IV.

Noise and ringing of the ears, which is called <term>aladaui</term> <gloss>tinnitus</gloss> and <term>althauin</term> <gloss>ringing of the ears</gloss>, occurs from an internal and external cause. The internal occurs for eight reasons: it is either from thick gas existing in the head rising from the stomach, or from a thick humor, or from a hot vapor existing in the head and rising from the stomach and the body, or from a weakness of hearing naturally or accidentally, or from some old disease, or from a disease occurring before the arrival of a crisis from a collection of putrid humor or phlegm or clotted blood, or from the fact that in time of health it was in a state of clarity of hearing and lightness of the head. The external cause is either from a plethora of much food and thick humor, or from inanition of laxatives or phlebotomy, or from a flux of blood or hunger from abstinence from food, or from much wine drinking, or from much vomiting, or from much swimming in water or submersion in it, or from those things that enter the ear or animals entering it.

The sign of a fullness of blood is redness of the face, heaviness of the head and forehead when one bends down, and the intensity of the throbbing; if the age, temperament, and season agree with this, it will be stronger. The sign of a hot humor is intense heat and inflammation of the ear, and the patient's delight in cool air; when the age, temperament, and season agree with this, it will be stronger. The sign of thick flatulence is a sensation of pulling or stretching and much ringing in the ear with lightness of the head. The sign of a pustule or abscess, which is called <term>almelas</term> <gloss>a severe ear abscess</gloss>, is intense pain, which is called <term>almelas</term>, and it is the strongest of all ear pains and the most dangerous, accompanied by pain in the entire forehead, head, and fever. The signs of obstruction from blood collected in the ear are heaviness of hearing and lightness of pain, and that you place the patient in the sun until the light of the eye falls upon it. The signs of the cause of tooth eruption in children are that the eruption is manifest, and if there is diarrhea. The signs of cold or heat and vapor offending the ear from the outside are those the patient reports, and because it happens after repetition. The sign from hot water entering the ear is that they entered a bath and that they feel the water. The sign from cold water is that they swam in it and feel the water when the head is moved. The sign of animals entering the ear is that sometimes they move and sometimes they do not, and it is with ringing and pain when that animal moves. The sign from the cause of that which enters, such as an animal, a small stone, or some other foreign object, is from what appears to the senses and examination of what the patient recounts. The sign of the cause of some hot or cold medicine is from the fact that the patient reports feeling heat or cold, and they feel cold with a heaviness of movement but do not feel pain. The sign from a blow or concussion is that it appears clearly and is grasped by the sensation of the impact. Nimrod the Tyrant lived until God took him at the age of two hundred years, and his death occurred in the month of April.

<margin>Serug son of Reu</margin>
When God took Reu, he was succeeded by Serug son of Reu. It is said that during his time, the worship of idols and images appeared, due to various reasons that emerged on Earth. He lived until God took him at the age of two hundred and thirty years.

<margin>Nahor son of Serug</margin>
When God took Serug, he was succeeded by his son Nahor son of Serug, who followed the example of his forefathers. In his days, tremors and earthquakes occurred, the likes of which had not been seen in previous times. Various crafts and instruments were invented during his era, and his time saw wars and the formation of factions in India and elsewhere. He lived until God took him at the age of one hundred and forty years.

<margin>Terah son of Nahor</margin>
When God took Nahor, he was succeeded by his son Terah, who is Azar, the father of Abraham the Friend of God. Nimrod son of Canaan lived during his era. In the days of Nimrod, the worship of fire and lights occurred on Earth, and hierarchies were established for their veneration. There was great chaos on Earth, with wars and the creation of cities and kingdoms in the East and West, and other such events. Statements regarding the decrees of the stars appeared, the celestial spheres were modeled, instruments were made for them, and an understanding of this was brought to the hearts of men. The astrologers observed the horoscope of the year in which Abraham, peace be upon him, was born and what it necessitated. They informed Nimrod that a child would be born who would invalidate their dreams and abolish their worship. Nimrod commanded that the male infants be killed, and Abraham, peace be upon him, was hidden in a cave. Azar, who is Terah, died, and he lived until God, may He be exalted and glorified, took him at the age of two hundred and seventy years. God is the grantor of success toward what is right.

[The scroll] that descends from God Almighty to the Angel of Death contains the name of the person whose soul is commanded to be taken, the location where it is to be taken, and the reason for the seizure. Abu al-Layth, may God have mercy on him, mentioned that two drops descend from beneath the Throne onto the name of their owner; one is green and the other is white. If the white one falls upon a name, it is known that he is blessed. If the green one falls upon a name, it is known that he is wretched.

As for the place where one dies, it is said that God Almighty created an angel entrusted with every newborn, called the Angel of the Wombs. When a person is born, he stirs within the drop of fluid in his mother's womb some of the earth's dust from the place where he will die. The servant then wanders wherever he wanders until he returns to the place of his earth and dies. This is indicated by the words of the Almighty: "Say, if you were in your houses, those who were decreed to be killed would have set out to their places of lying down."

In this regard, it is recounted that the Angel of Death used to appear in earlier times. One day, he entered upon Solomon, son of David—peace be upon them both—and stared intensely at a young man sitting with him. The young man trembled before him. When the Angel of Death departed, the young man said, "O Prophet of God, I want you to command the wind to carry me to <column-break/> China."

Solomon commanded the wind, and it carried him to China. The Angel of Death returned to Solomon, who remained silent, then asked him about his staring at the young man. He said, "O Prophet of God, I was commanded to take his soul this very day in China. I saw him with you and was astonished by that." Solomon then told him the story of how the youth had asked him to command the wind to carry him to China. The Angel of Death said, "I took his soul this very day in China."

According to another report, the Angel of Death had assistants who performed the task of taking souls. It is narrated that a man was inspired to say, "O God, forgive me and the Angel of the Sun." This angel asked his Lord for permission to visit him. When he descended to him, he said, "You invoke God for me often, so what is your need?" He replied, "My need is for you to carry me to your place and to ask the Angel of Death to inform me of the approach of my term." He carried him and sat him in his place in the sun, then ascended to the Angel of Death and mentioned the matter to him, saying that a man from the sons of Adam was inspired to say, every time he prayed, "O God, forgive me and the Angel of the Sun," and that he requested me to ask you to inform him when his term is near so that he might prepare for it. The Angel of Death looked into the book of his term and said, "Indeed, your companion..."

# Decisive Treatise: On the Connection Between Philosophy and the Law

Harm from a friend is more severe than harm from an enemy. I mean that philosophy is the companion of the Law and its foster sister. Therefore, harm coming from those who attribute themselves to it is the most severe of harm, especially considering the enmity, hatred, and quarreling that occur between them, even though they are by nature companions and by essence and instinct lovers of one another. Many ignorant friends, who attribute themselves to it, have also harmed it; these are the sects found within it. May God guide everyone, grant them success in loving Him, unite their hearts in piety toward Him, and remove from them hatred and animosity by His grace and mercy. God has removed many of these evils, ignorances, and misleading paths through this overarching matter, and has paved the way through it to many good things, especially for the class of people who have followed the path of rational inquiry and desired to know the Truth. For He has called the masses to a middle path for knowing God, one that rises above the abyss of the imitators and descends from the agitation of the <term>Mutakallimun</term> <gloss>theological dialecticians</gloss>, and He has alerted the elite to the necessity of complete inquiry into the origin of the Law.

## ۞ An Appendix to the Question of Divine Knowledge, which Abu al-Walid <note>Averroes</note> mentioned in the Decisive Treatise, may God be pleased with him ۞

May God perpetuate your glory, sustain your blessing, and shield your eyes from calamities. Since you have surpassed many who engage in these sciences through the excellence of your mind and the nobility of your character, and your sound vision has reached the point of identifying the doubt that arises regarding the knowledge of the Eternal, glorified is He, given that it relates to created things, it has become incumbent upon us, for the sake of the Truth and for the sake of removing this suspicion from you, to resolve this doubt after we state its formulation. For he who does not know how to tie a knot cannot untie it. Harm from a friend is more severe than harm from an enemy. I mean that wisdom is the companion of the law <note>original: "الشريعة"</note> and its foster sister. Therefore, the harm coming from those who attribute themselves to it is the most severe of all, especially given the enmity, hatred, and contention that occur between them, even though they are by nature companions and, in their essence and instinct, lovers of one another.

It has also been harmed by many ignorant friends—those who count themselves among its followers—and by the sects found within it. May God guide all, grant everyone success in His love, unite their hearts in His piety, and remove hatred and malice from them by His grace and mercy. God has already removed many of these evils, ignorances, and misleading paths through this prevailing command, and has opened through it a way to many good things. This is especially true for the class of people who have followed the path of inquiry and desired to know the truth. For he has called the masses from a knowledge of God to a middle path, one that rises above the lowest level of the followers of tradition <term>muqallidun</term> <gloss>those who accept dogma without inquiry</gloss> and descends below the disturbances of the dialectical theologians <term>mutakallimun</term> <gloss>practitioners of speculative theology</gloss>. He also alerted the elite to the necessity of complete inquiry into the root of the law.
